extracted.intended_audience: patent owners, patent practitioners, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and quality/formal requirements for preparing and submitting amendments (to specification, claims, and drawings) in ex parte and inter partes reexamination proceedings before the USPTO, including formatting, marking, claim status, support, numbering, timing, and handling when patents have been previously amended or expire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markings for changes (deletions/additions)
rubrics_metrics.description: All changes relative to the patent being reexamined which are made to the specification, including the claims, must include markings: matter to be omitted must be enclosed in brackets; matter to be added must be underlined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Markings are made in comparison to the original patent (not to any prior amendment). Underlining for additions will be printed as italics in the reexamination certificate and brackets are printed as inserted in the proceeding. 37 CFR 1.530(f) identifies these marking types; added paragraphs must be submitted completely underlined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of claims and explanation of support
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever there is an amendment to the claims, the status (pending or canceled) of all patent claims and added claims as of the date of the amendment must be supplied on pages separate from the changes, together with an explanation of the support in the disclosure of the patent for the changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to submit claim status generally results in an informal response to the patent owner prior to final rejection; an amendment submitted after final rejection lacking this will not be entered. Explanations of support go to the merits and must cite where support exists in the specification (examples show column/line citations in Remarks).

rubrics_metrics.name: No renumbering of original patent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Original patent claim numbers may not be changed; a patent claim retains its number even if canceled in the reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbering of any added claims must begin after the highest-numbered original patent claim. A claim number previously assigned to a new claim that has been canceled should not be reassigned to a different new claim during the reexamination proceeding; renumbering for final certificate may occur to compress finalized new claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: No enlargement of claim scope / no new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may enlarge the scope of the claims of the patent or introduce new matter. No amendment may be proposed for entry in an expired patent; no amendment (other than cancellation) will be incorporated into the patent by a certificate issued after expiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amended or new claims that broaden scope should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 305. Proposed amendments are treated as entered by Office actions for prosecution purposes but are not effective until the reexamination certificate is issued and published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments not effective until reexamination certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: Although Office actions will treat proposed amendments as though they have been entered, the proposed amendments will not be effective in the patent until the reexamination certificate is issued and published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This affects enforceability and timing; if the patent expires before certificate issuance, amendments will not be incorporated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal paper requirements (37 CFR 1.52) for submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers to become part of permanent USPTO records must be on sheets of specified sizes (A4 or 8.5x11), single-sided, unbound, white, flexible, with specified margins (top ≥2.0 cm, left ≥2.5 cm, right ≥2.0 cm, bottom ≥2.0 cm), and plainly/legibly written by typewriter or machine printer in permanent dark ink.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text must have sufficient clarity/contrast for reproduction and OCR. Preferably 12-point nonscript fonts (Arial, Times Roman, Courier); lines 1.5 or double spaced for specifications; single column text. Claims must commence on separate physical sheet/electronic page; abstract on separate sheet or first page in reissue/reexamination. See 37 CFR 1.52 for full specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing and formatting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers submitted electronically must be formatted and transmitted in compliance with USPTO patent electronic filing system requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow USPTO EFS technical and formatting rules; other 1.52 formatting rules may not apply to pre-printed Office forms or to certain double-column patent copies used as specifications for reissue or reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification amendment presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: All amendments to the specification (other than claims/drawings) must be made by submission of the entire text of each added or rewritten paragraph with markings (single brackets for deletions, underlining for additions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The only exception is deleting an entire paragraph by statement deleting it without presenting the paragraph text, although presenting the text aids proper entry. The precise point where any added/rewritten paragraph is located must be indicated; uncertainty may delay issuance of the reexamination certificate. Examiner amendments at NIRC also require the full text with markings; 1.121(g) exception does not apply in reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims amendment presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: For each claim proposed to be amended, the entire text of the claim must be presented with appropriate markings; for each proposed new claim, the entire text must be presented and underlined throughout; canceled claims require a direction to cancel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bracketing for deletions and underlining for additions are required. Examiner's amendments at NIRC require full-text presentation with markings. If a patent claim dependency is to be changed, it is proper to make that original patent claim dependent upon a later-filed higher-numbered claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accompanying explanation of support for claim changes (per 1.530(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each claim amendment must be accompanied by an explanation of the support in the disclosure of the patent for the amendment (support for any insertions and deletions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to submit the explanation generally results in notification that the amendment prior to final rejection is not completely responsive; amendments submitted after final rejection without support explanation will not be entered. Examples show required 'Remarks' pages listing status and specific column/line support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation rules for new claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposed new claim should be presented with underlining throughout the claim, including the claim number; the status identifier '(new)' may or may not be underlined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners may accept minor deviations (e.g., claim number not underlined). Added claims are numbered beginning after the last original patent claim; if new claims are later canceled, remaining new claims will be renumbered for the NIRC/certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of new claims (no bracketing vs prior amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment of a new claim (previously presented in the reexamination) must present the entire text of the new claim containing the amendatory material and must be underlined throughout; the presentation cannot contain any bracketing or other indication of what was in the previous version of the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner must point out what is changed in the 'Remarks' portion of the amendment and provide support citations. All changes in reexamination are made vis-à-vis the original patent, not in comparison with any prior amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple amendments to original patent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When an original patent claim is amended more than once, each subsequent amendment must include the changes previously presented plus the new changes, and present the entire claim only with changes from the original patent text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Words that were added in earlier amendments but not part of the original patent text are deleted by simply omitting them (not bracketed) in later amendments. Words replaced in earlier amendments are shown as deleted/added only in comparison to the original patent text (examples illustrate twice-amended claim formatting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings amendment procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Any change to the patent drawings must be submitted as a sketch on a separate paper showing the proposed changes in red for approval by the examiner; after approval, new sheets of drawings for each sheet changed must be filed and comply with 37 CFR 1.84.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amended figures must be identified as 'Amended', added figures as 'New', and canceled figures surrounded by brackets and identified as 'Canceled.' Changes may NOT be made on original patent drawings. If a new sheet contains multiple figures, each figure must be marked 'amended' or 'new' as applicable; it is insufficient to only mark the header. Submit an 'Annotated Sheet' sketch which becomes part of record. New sheets must be entered into record prior to NIRC preparation; if approved but not filed, prepare a Quayle action (set SSP one month or two months depending on requester) or certificate may issue without the proposed drawing changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of amendments when prior post-patent proceedings changed patent
rubrics_metrics.description: When a prior concluded post-patent proceeding (e.g., prior reexamination certificate, reissue, certificate of correction, PTAB trial certificate) has changed the patent, the first amendment must be made relative to the patent specification as changed by the prior proceeding; subsequent amendments must be made relative to the patent specification in effect as of the filing of the request for reexamination (not relative to prior amendment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For pending reexaminations where a certificate or reissue exists, present italicized text of the certificate/reissue as if present without italics in the original patent, and omit any text that was in brackets in that certificate/reissue. Similar rules apply for PTAB trial certificates and merged proceedings; see cross-referenced MPEP sections for specific situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of patent expiration during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent expires during the pendency of a reexamination proceeding, no amendment may be proposed for entry in an expired patent; all amendments to the patent claims and all claims added during the proceeding are withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will hold amendments to be improper and subsequent reexamination will be on the basis of the unamended patent claims. The cancellation of original patent claims is the only 'amendatory' change permitted in an expired patent; examiner should ensure all rejected/objected claims are canceled before issuing NIRC (issue examiner's amendment canceling such claims if necessary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal/improper amendment handling and statutory periods (form paragraphs)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment does not comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j), a supplemental paper correctly proposing amendments is required; a shortened statutory period (SSP) is set to correct the informality (ONE MONTH or thirty days, whichever is longer if requested by third party; TWO MONTHS if requested by patent owner or Director-ordered/reexamination under 35 U.S.C. 257).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraphs 22.12 to advise proper manner and 22.13 to advise of improper amendment; if the informality is not timely corrected the amendment may be held not to be an appropriate response and prosecution may be terminated with a reexamination certificate issued. After final rejection, an amendment lacking proper form should not be entered and patent owner informed using Form PTOL-467.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special handling for large tables, sequence listings, and program listings
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to 'Large Tables' (ASCII plain text), a 'Computer Program Listing Appendix', a 'Sequence Listing', or a 'Sequence Listing XML' must be made in accordance with the specific CFR provisions for those items (37 CFR 1.58(g), 1.96(c)(5), 1.825, 1.835 respectively).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.530(d)(1)(ii) states that 1.530(d)(1)(i) is not to be used for making amendments to these specialized items; follow the applicable section for format and submission rules.
